scanNote:
GRAMMAR REFERENCE, 8-BET (123-bet). Yuqorida o'ngda 'Grammar Reference'.

CHAP USTUN:
'PRESENT PERFECT vs PAST SIMPLE': • We use the present perfect for an action which started in the past and continues to the present. 'He has called twice so far.' • We use the past simple for an action which started and finished in the past. 'He called yesterday.'
'PRESENT PERFECT CONTINUOUS'. KO'K JADVAL: Affirmative: I've been reading, you've been reading, he's been reading, she's been reading, it's been reading, we've been reading, you've been reading, they've been reading. Interrogative: Have I been reading? Have you been reading? Has he been reading? ... Have they been reading? Negative: I haven't been reading, you haven't been reading, he hasn't been reading, ... they haven't been reading. Short answers: Yes, I/you/we/they have. he/she/it has. No, I/you/we/they haven't. he/she/it hasn't.
'Form': • We form the present perfect continuous with the auxiliary verb have/has, the past participle of the verb to be (been) and the main verb with the -ing form. 'He has been watching TV for an hour.' • We form questions by putting have/has before the subject. 'Have you been working here long?' • We form negations by putting not between have/has and been. 'They have not/haven't been studying for a long time. She has not/hasn't been living here long.'

O'NG USTUN:
'Use': • We use the present perfect continuous to talk about an action which started in the past and continues to the present giving emphasis to duration. 'He has been going to Jamaica for his holidays since 1993.' • We also use the present perfect continuous to talk about a past action which has lasted and whose result is visible in the present. 'I'm tired because I've been studying for my exam.'
Ko'k 'UNIT 8'. 'PAST PERFECT SIMPLE'. KO'K JADVAL: Affirmative: I had started, you had started, he had started, ... they had started. Interrogative: Had I started? Had you started? ... Had they started? Negative: I hadn't started, ... they hadn't started. Short answers: Yes, I/you/he etc had. No, I/you/he etc hadn't.
'Form': • We form the past perfect simple with had and the past participle of the main verb. • We form questions by putting had before the subject. • We form negations by putting not after had.
'Use': 'We use the past perfect simple for a past action which happened in the past before another past action. He watched TV after he had finished his homework. (First, he finished his homework, then he watched TV.)'

Bet raqami: pastda o'ngda '123'.

exercises.instructionEn: Present Perfect vs Past Simple. We use the present perfect for an action which started in the past and continues to the present. He has called twice so far. We use the past simple for an action which started and finished in the past. He called yesterday.
exercises.instructionUz: Present Perfect va Past Simple. Hozirgi tugallangan zamonni o'tmishda boshlanib hozirgacha davom etayotgan ish uchun ishlatamiz. U hozirgacha ikki marta qo'ng'iroq qildi. O'tgan oddiy zamonni o'tmishda boshlanib tugagan ish uchun ishlatamiz. U kecha qo'ng'iroq qildi.
exercises.explanationUz:
PRESENT PERFECT va PAST SIMPLE
FARQI:

  PRESENT PERFECT:
    O'tmishda boshlangan, HOZIR
    bilan BOG'LIQ.
    'He HAS CALLED twice SO FAR.'
    (hozirgacha - yana qo'ng'iroq
    qilishi mumkin)
    Vaqt: so far, just, already,
    yet, ever, never, for, since

  PAST SIMPLE:
    O'tmishda boshlanib TUGAGAN,
    ANIQ VAQT bilan.
    'He CALLED YESTERDAY.'
    Vaqt: yesterday, last week, ago,
    in 1998

  ⚠ 'yesterday' bilan HECh QAChON
  present perfect ishlatilmaydi:
  "I've called yesterday" ✗.

exercises.instructionEn: Present Perfect Continuous. Affirmative: I've been reading, he's been reading. Interrogative: Have I been reading? Has he been reading? Negative: I haven't been reading. Short answers: Yes, I have. / No, he hasn't. Form: have/has + been + -ing. Use: an action which started in the past and continues to the present giving emphasis to duration; a past action which has lasted and whose result is visible in the present.
exercises.instructionUz: Hozirgi tugallangan davomli zamon. Tasdiq: I've been reading, he's been reading. So'roq: Have I been reading? Has he been reading? Inkor: I haven't been reading. Qisqa javoblar: Yes, I have. / No, he hasn't. Shakli: have/has + been + -ing. Ishlatilishi: o'tmishda boshlanib hozirgacha davom etayotgan ish - davomiylikka urg'u; natijasi hozir ko'rinadigan davom etgan o'tgan ish.
exercises.explanationUz:
PRESENT PERFECT CONTINUOUS.

  HAVE / HAS + BEEN + FE'L-ING


╔══════════════════════════════════╗
║  ShAKLI                          ║
╚══════════════════════════════════╝

  TASDIQ: I've been reading, he's
    been reading
  SO'ROQ: Have you been working
    here long?
  INKOR: They haven't been
    studying. She hasn't been
    living here long.
  QISQA: Yes, I have. / No, he
    hasn't.

  ⚠ 'not' - have/has va 'been'
  ORASIDA.


╔══════════════════════════════════╗
║  IShLATILIShI                    ║
╚══════════════════════════════════╝

  1 O'tmishda boshlanib hozirgacha
    davom etayotgan ish -
    DAVOMIYLIKKA URG'U:
    'He HAS BEEN GOING to Jamaica
     since 1993.'
    'He has been watching TV FOR
     AN HOUR.'

  2 Davom etgan o'tgan ish -
    NATIJASI HOZIR KO'RINADI:
    "I'm tired because I'VE BEEN
     STUDYING for my exam."
    (charchoq - natija)


⚠ PRESENT PERFECT bilan FARQI:

  Present perfect - NATIJA/SON:
    "I've read three books."
  Present perfect continuous -
  JARAYoN/DAVOMIYLIK:
    "I've been reading all day."


⚠ 'EMPHASIS':

  = urg'u.


⚠ 'TO LAST':

  = davom etmoq.

points.en: We form the present perfect continuous with the auxiliary verb have/has, the past participle of the verb to be (been) and the main verb with the -ing form. He has been watching TV for an hour.
points.uz: Hozirgi tugallangan davomli zamonni yordamchi fe'l have/has, 'to be' fe'lining 3-shakli (been) va asosiy fe'lning -ing shakli bilan yasaymiz. U bir soatdan beri televizor ko'rmoqda.

points.en: We form questions by putting have/has before the subject. Have you been working here long? We form negations by putting not between have/has and been. They have not/haven't been studying for a long time. She has not/hasn't been living here long.
points.uz: Savollarni have/has ni egadan oldin qo'yib yasaymiz. Bu yerda uzoqdan beri ishlayapsizmi? Inkorni have/has va been orasiga not qo'yib yasaymiz. Ular uzoq vaqtdan beri o'qimayapti. U bu yerda uzoqdan beri yashamayapti.

points.en: We use the present perfect continuous to talk about an action which started in the past and continues to the present giving emphasis to duration. He has been going to Jamaica for his holidays since 1993.
points.uz: Hozirgi tugallangan davomli zamonni o'tmishda boshlanib hozirgacha davom etayotgan ish haqida davomiylikka urg'u berib gapirish uchun ishlatamiz. U 1993 yildan beri ta'tilga Yamaykaga bormoqda.

points.en: We also use the present perfect continuous to talk about a past action which has lasted and whose result is visible in the present. I'm tired because I've been studying for my exam.
points.uz: Hozirgi tugallangan davomli zamonni natijasi hozir ko'rinadigan davom etgan o'tgan ish haqida gapirish uchun ham ishlatamiz. Charchadim, chunki imtihonga tayyorlanayotgan edim.

exercises.instructionEn: Past Perfect Simple. Affirmative: I had started. Interrogative: Had I started? Negative: I hadn't started. Short answers: Yes, I had. / No, I hadn't. Form: had + past participle. Use: a past action which happened before another past action. He watched TV after he had finished his homework.
exercises.instructionUz: O'tgan tugallangan zamon. Tasdiq: I had started. So'roq: Had I started? Inkor: I hadn't started. Qisqa javoblar: Yes, I had. / No, I hadn't. Shakli: had + 3-shakl. Ishlatilishi: boshqa o'tgan ishdan oldin bo'lgan o'tgan ish. U uy vazifasini tugatgandan keyin televizor ko'rdi.
exercises.explanationUz:
PAST PERFECT - O'TMIShDAN OLDINGI
O'TMISh.

  HAD + FE'LNING 3-ShAKLI
  (HAMMA shaxsda bir xil!)


╔══════════════════════════════════╗
║  ShAKLI                          ║
╚══════════════════════════════════╝

  TASDIQ: I had started = I'd
    started; he had started
  SO'ROQ: Had he started?
  INKOR: He hadn't started.
  QISQA: Yes, I had. / No, I
    hadn't.


╔══════════════════════════════════╗
║  IShLATILIShI                    ║
╚══════════════════════════════════╝

  O'tmishdagi IKKI ish - qaysi
  OLDIN bo'lgan:
  'He WATCHED TV after he HAD
   FINISHED his homework.'
  1-ish (oldin): had finished
  2-ish (keyin): watched

  ⚠ 'after', 'before', 'when',
  'by the time' bilan ko'p keladi.


⚠ KO'ChIRMA GAPDA:

  Past simple → past perfect:
  'She left' → 'He said she HAD
  LEFT.' (14-unit)


⚠ "I'D":

  = I had (past perfect) yoki I
  would - kontekstga qarang:
  "I'd finished" (had),
  "I'd like" (would).

points.en: Affirmative: I had started, he had started, they had started. Interrogative: Had I started? Had he started? Negative: I hadn't started, he hadn't started. Short answers: Yes, I/you/he etc had. No, I/you/he etc hadn't.
points.uz: Tasdiq: I had started, he had started, they had started. So'roq: Had I started? Had he started? Inkor: I hadn't started, he hadn't started. Qisqa javoblar: Yes, I/you/he etc had. No, I/you/he etc hadn't.

points.en: We form the past perfect simple with had and the past participle of the main verb. We form questions by putting had before the subject. We form negations by putting not after had.
points.uz: O'tgan tugallangan zamonni had va asosiy fe'lning 3-shakli bilan yasaymiz. Savollarni had ni egadan oldin qo'yib yasaymiz. Inkorni had dan keyin not qo'yib yasaymiz.

points.en: We use the past perfect simple for a past action which happened in the past before another past action. He watched TV after he had finished his homework. (First, he finished his homework, then he watched TV.)
points.uz: O'tgan tugallangan zamonni boshqa o'tgan ishdan oldin bo'lgan o'tgan ish uchun ishlatamiz. U uy vazifasini tugatgandan keyin televizor ko'rdi. (Avval uy vazifasini tugatdi, keyin televizor ko'rdi.)
